indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.2.1 Know common diseases of humans; causes, symptoms, effects and prevention
indicator.objective: Identify causes, symptoms and prevention of cholera

skills.description: Recognise that cholera is caused by germs from contaminated food or water.
Identify common symptoms of cholera (e.g. serious diarrhoea, vomiting, dehydration).
Describe how cholera spreads (drinking contaminated water, eating contaminated food, poor sanitation).
Identify ways to prevent cholera (drinking safe water, washing hands, proper waste disposal, covering food).
State what to do if someone shows signs of cholera (give safe water, see a health worker immediately).
Organise causes, symptoms and prevention of cholera in a simple table or map.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Cholera is spread through the air.
Cholera is the same as malaria.
Cholera is caused by eating too much food.

questions.stem: What causes cholera?
options: Germs from contaminated food or water
hints: Cholera is linked to dirty water.
It is caused by tiny germs.
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by germs that come from contaminated food or water.
questions.misconception: Cholera is caused by eating too much food.

questions.stem: A learner says, 'Cholera is spread through the air like a cold.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, cholera spreads through the air
No, cholera spreads mainly through contaminated water and food
No, cholera is caused by malaria
No, cholera cannot spread at all
hints: Think about dirty water and food.
Cholera is not an airborne disease.
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads mainly through drinking contaminated water or eating contaminated food, not through the air.
questions.misconception: Cholera is spread through the air.

questions.stem: What causes cholera?
answer: germs from contaminated food or water
hints: Think about dirty water.
Germs cause it.
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by germs found in contaminated food or water.
questions.misconception: Cholera is caused by bad air.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common symptom of cholera?
hints: Cholera affects the stomach and toilet habits.
It causes watery stool.
questions.explanation: Serious diarrhoea is a common symptom of cholera.
questions.misconception: Cholera causes toothache.

questions.stem: Which set lists common symptoms of cholera?
hints: Cholera causes watery stool and vomiting.
The body loses a lot of water.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of cholera include diarrhoea, vomiting and dehydration.
questions.misconception: Cholera only causes a rash.

questions.stem: Name two symptoms of cholera.
hints: One is watery stool.
Another is throwing up.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of cholera are diarrhoea and vomiting. Dehydration also occurs.
questions.misconception: Cholera has no symptoms.

questions.stem: Why is dehydration dangerous for a person with cholera?
options: The body loses too much water and salts
The body gains too much water
The body produces too much blood
hints: Diarrhoea and vomiting remove water from the body.
The body needs water to function.
questions.explanation: Dehydration is dangerous because the body loses too much water and salts, which can lead to serious health problems.
questions.misconception: Dehydration is not serious.

questions.stem: How can cholera spread from one person to another?
hints: Cholera germs are in dirty water.
People get it from what they eat or drink.
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads when people drink contaminated water or eat contaminated food.
questions.misconception: Cholera spreads through the air.

questions.stem: Which of these can help cholera spread?
options: Drinking water from a dirty stream
Covering food with a clean cloth
hints: Dirty water contains germs.
Which action brings germs into the body?
questions.explanation: Drinking water from a dirty stream can spread cholera because the water contains germs.
questions.misconception: Cholera is not spread by water.

questions.stem: Describe one way cholera can spread.
answer: drinking water from a dirty source
hints: Think about dirty water.
Think about food that flies have touched.
questions.explanation: Cholera can spread through drinking contaminated water or eating contaminated food.
questions.misconception: Cholera spreads through the air.

questions.stem: Which of these helps prevent cholera?
hints: Safe water is free from germs.
Boiling water makes it safe.
questions.explanation: Drinking safe water helps prevent cholera because it does not contain cholera germs.
questions.misconception: Any water is safe to drink.

questions.stem: Which of these is a good way to prevent cholera?
options: Washing hands with soap before eating
Eating food that has been left uncovered
hints: Clean hands have fewer germs.
Soap removes germs.
questions.explanation: Washing hands with soap before eating helps prevent cholera by removing germs.
questions.misconception: Hand washing is not important.

questions.stem: Give one way to prevent cholera.
hints: Think about clean water.
Think about hand washing.
questions.explanation: Ways to prevent cholera include drinking safe water, washing hands with soap, and covering food.
questions.misconception: Cholera cannot be prevented.

questions.stem: A family collects water from a river. What should they do to make it safe to drink?
options: Let the water settle and drink it
hints: Boiling kills germs.
River water can contain cholera germs.
questions.explanation: Boiling river water kills cholera germs and makes it safe to drink.
questions.misconception: River water is always safe.

questions.stem: A learner has serious diarrhoea and vomiting. What should you do?
options: Tell an adult and take the learner to a health worker
hints: Serious diarrhoea can be cholera.
A health worker can help.
questions.explanation: You should tell an adult and take the learner to a health worker immediately.
questions.misconception: Cholera does not need medical help.

questions.stem: What should you do if someone shows signs of cholera?
answer: give them safe water and take them to a health worker
tell an adult and see a health worker
give safe water and seek medical help
hints: The person needs water.
They need medical attention.
questions.explanation: Give the person safe water to drink and take them to a health worker immediately.
questions.misconception: You should wait for cholera to go away.

questions.stem: A cholera patient is very thirsty and weak. What is the most important first step?
options: Give them safe water to drink
hints: Cholera causes dehydration.
The body needs water.
questions.explanation: Giving safe water is the most important first step to replace lost fluids and prevent severe dehydration.
questions.misconception: Cholera patients should not drink water.

questions.stem: Draw a simple table with three columns: 'Causes', 'Symptoms' and 'Prevention'. Write at least one correct point under each column for cholera.

criteria.description: Wrote one correct cause of cholera
Wrote one correct symptom of cholera
Wrote one correct way to prevent cholera
Organised the points clearly under the three headings

hints: Think about dirty water for causes.
Think about diarrhoea for symptoms.
Think about boiling water for prevention.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Cholera has no clear causes or prevention.

questions.stem: Design a simple poster to teach your class about cholera. Show one cause, one symptom and one way to prevent it. Use drawings and short words.

criteria.description: Showed one correct cause of cholera
Showed one correct symptom of cholera
Showed one correct way to prevent cholera
Used drawings and short words clearly

hints: Draw dirty water for a cause.
Draw a sick person for a symptom.
Draw soap and water for prevention.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Cholera cannot be prevented.

questions.stem: Complete this sentence: Cholera is caused by ______ and can be prevented by ______.
answer: germs from contaminated water, drinking safe water
germs in dirty water, washing hands
contaminated food and water, boiling water
hints: First blank: what causes it?
Second blank: how to stop it?
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by germs from contaminated water or food and can be prevented by drinking safe water and washing hands.
questions.misconception: Cholera has no cause or prevention.
